title: Accrual and Crediting of Interest on Certificates of Deposit
content:
Interest on a certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line accrues daily, is credited on the dates the tier publishes, and is then either added to the principal or sent to another Piedmont Crescent account.

## 1. Daily accrual

Interest accrues on every calendar day from the term start date through the day before the maturity date. A day's accrual is the principal standing at the end of that day multiplied by the interest rate the certificate carries, divided by one hundred and divided by the days the tier publishes as its year. Because compounding is daily on every tier of this line, each day's accrual joins the base on which the next day accrues.

*Hypothetical:* principal 10000.00 USD at the end of the day, a rate of 4.05 percent and a year of 365 days. Ten thousand multiplied by 4.05, divided by one hundred, gives 405.00; divided by 365, the day's accrual is 1.1096 USD and so on, and the next day accrues on that principal increased by the day's accrual, the figure joining the base as it stands.

## 2. Crediting

Where the tier credits monthly, accrued interest is credited on the last calendar day of each month, and on the maturity date for the final part-month. Where the tier credits at maturity, it is credited once, on the maturity date. The amount credited for a period is the unrounded accrual for that period rounded to the nearest cent with a half rounded up.

## 3. Disposition of the credit

| Disposition chosen | Effect on the certificate | Effect on another account |
|---|---|---|
| compounded | the principal rises by the credit | none |
| paid to a Piedmont Crescent checking account | the principal is unchanged | that account is credited |
| paid to a Piedmont Crescent savings or money market account | the principal is unchanged | that account is credited |

Only the dispositions the tier lists may be chosen. An account receiving paid-out interest must belong to the same customer and be active; where it is not, the interest for that period compounds instead.

## 4. Interest at a full early withdrawal and across a maturity

Interest accrued but not yet credited is credited on the day of a full early withdrawal, before the penalty is worked out.

During the grace period, a balance that is withdrawn earns no interest for the grace days on a tier that does not let grace days earn interest on a withdrawn balance. A balance that renews earns the new term's rate from the maturity date onward.
